properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — surfaced by the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review, but NOT a new idea: this question already exists as PROSE in docs/requirements-coverage.md ("Note: are embeddings (an embeddings-rs sidecar) actually needed?"). Recording it here moves it from a document into the graph, which is the direction dec:what-lives-where argues for; it does not settle it. STILL OPEN.

WHAT IS AVAILABLE AND UNUSED: dynograph-vector ships an HNSW approximate-nearest-neighbour index (HnswConfig / HnswIndex / SearchResult, with filtered, batch and snapshot-persisted search) plus SIMD cosine similarity and the whole distance family. reflow2 uses none of it. search_design is BM25 lexical, and the schema carries embedding_field declarations on several node types that nothing populates.

THE CASE FOR: semantic search would find a requirement whose words differ from the query's. It would also strengthen resolution — the duplicate-detection path already has a fuzzy_then_vector strategy declared in the schema with the vector half unimplemented.

THE CASE AGAINST, and it is why this has stayed parked: embeddings need a MODEL, and reflow2-core is deliberately LLM-free and deterministic. An embedding provider at the core would break that, and putting it at the seam means a sidecar to install, version and keep in sync — which cuts against req:thin-install and the whole served-not-installed posture. Determinism is also load-bearing here: two runs of a detector must agree, and an ANN index is approximate by construction.

--- 2026-08-04, re-examined while building BL-186 (cap:corpus-ingest). Four things are now MEASURED rather than supposed, and one distinction is offered against the case-against. The question is still open and this update does not settle it. ---

1. THE PRODUCER EXISTS AND IS ANTHONY'S OWN. `embeddings-rs` (github.com/sligara7/embeddings-rs, local at a990e4d v0.1.1) is a Rust/ONNX parity sidecar for nomic-embed-text-v1.5 with a code-derived, drift-gated OpenAPI contract, written to pair with dynograph-foundation. That matters to the case-against: "a provider dependency" and "a local, self-hosted, contract-frozen sidecar you maintain" are not the same risk, and the deferral's stated reason was avoiding an external LLM provider.

2. THE WHOLE PATH EXISTS AND IS INERT — VERIFIED, not read from the earlier note. dynograph-storage has an embeddings column family with set_embedding / get_embedding / delete_embedding / scan_embeddings_by_type. dynograph-vector really does ship HNSW (crates/dynograph-vector/src/hnsw.rs) and SIMD cosine (distance.rs). reflow2's own schema declares embedding_field on Capability, Requirement, Question and others. reflow2's source contains exactly two matches for "embedding": a bidi-sanitizer comment and a doc comment saying "no embeddings". So the missing piece was never the model or the index — it is reflow2 calling any of it. embedding_field is another declared-and-read-by-nothing field, this time spanning four components.

3. NOT NEEDED FOR cap:corpus-ingest, AND ANTHONY SCOPED IT OUT ON 2026-08-04: "keep BL-186 lexical and ship it." The cost half of the corpus problem is candidate generation, which the BM25 index already in the served binary answers; embeddings would ADD a round trip per node, not remove one. The ordering half was a naming bug, fixed lexically. The folder driver needs no vectors.

4. WHERE IT WOULD ACTUALLY EARN ITS KEEP, and this is the honest limit of the lexical answer: req:corpus-ingest requires that "the same component named in forty specifications must converge on one node". Forty authors do not merely reorder tokens, they choose different words. token_sort_ratio cannot see "Read Cache" ~ "Local Store" at all — that is not a low score, it is invisible. The cases the scope doc names (Auth Service / Authentication Service = 84, Gateway / API Gateway = 74) are the EASY ones because they still share tokens. So shipping BL-186 lexical satisfies the requirement's ordering clause and its cost, and leaves its convergence clause satisfied only for documents that happen to share vocabulary. That limit should be stated to a user pointing reflow2 at a heterogeneous corpus rather than discovered by them.

5. THE DISTINCTION OFFERED AGAINST THE CASE-AGAINST: determinism is treated above as one blanket objection — "two runs of a detector must agree, and an ANN index is approximate by construction". That is strong for search_design and for anything feeding a gate. It is materially weaker for INGEST RESOLUTION, because under dec:ask-not-repair that path's output is a merge_candidate a human rules on, not a verdict. Approximate retrieval feeding a QUESTION is a different risk from approximate retrieval feeding a GATE. So the answer may not be a single yes/no: "yes, on the ingest resolution path only" would leave req:deterministic-core intact. Offered as a distinction to consider, not as advocacy — the req:thin-install objection stands unchanged either way, since a sidecar to install, version and keep in sync is a real change to the one-binary deployment story.

--- 2026-08-06: FIRST EXTERNAL EVIDENCE. Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 survey of the "graph brain" ecosystem (relayed by Anthony), recorded here because it bears on the case-against and on nothing else in the node. Does not settle the question. ---

6. EVERY COMPARABLE SYSTEM IN THE FIELD IS HYBRID, NOT LEXICAL. Mem0 combines vector search with graph relations and key-value storage; Cognee's pipeline is ingest, chunk, entity/relationship extraction, then vector DB plus graph DB plus relational, queried by hybrid graph-and-semantic similarity; Zep/Graphiti, Letta, LangMem and LlamaIndex Memory all rest on vector retrieval. Not one of the surveyed systems is retrieval-lexical-only. That does not make lexical wrong — none of those systems has reflow2's determinism requirement, because none of them feeds a GATE, which is precisely the distinction drawn in point 5 — but it does mean the case-against can no longer include "nobody needs this": everyone building in this space has paid for it. The question narrows to whether reflow2's gate-feeding, one-binary posture is worth the retrieval quality it costs, and that is a real trade rather than an oversight.

7. WHAT THE COMPARISON DOES NOT SHOW: none of those systems has to answer a query the same way twice, and none of them exports a byte-stable artifact a CI gate diffs. So their unanimity is weak evidence about reflow2's core and strong evidence only about the ingest-resolution path — exactly where point 5 already located the weaker objection. The external evidence therefore sharpens the existing distinction rather than adding a new argument.

--- 2026-09-22: THE LEXICAL LIMIT COST SOMETHING ON REFLOW2'S OWN GRAPH, AND A THIRD OPTION THIS NODE DOES NOT HOLD. Still open; this does not settle it. ---

8. **THE FIRST MEASURED COST HERE, RATHER THAN ON A HYPOTHETICAL CORPUS.** Point 4 located the lexical limit in `req:corpus-ingest` — forty authors choosing different words for one component — and framed it as something to state to a user pointing reflow2 at a heterogeneous corpus. It arrived on THIS design instead. Anthony described his founding chain in narrative English ("testing discovers a failure → … → go back to the decision point or fork and say, we need to go in a different direction"). Searching his exact words, measured:

       FOUND on his wording:     dec:idea-lifecycle-dimensions-on-a-requirement,
                                 dec:idea-cost-to-change-is-read-from-lifecycle-phase,
                                 cap:recover-from-tests, req:scenarios-are-modelled
       NOT FOUND until he used
       the words "fork" and
       "decision point":         cap:revise-trigger, cap:fork-alternatives,
                                 req:roads-not-taken, dec:reopen-supersedes,
                                 dec:fork-point-address, dec:alternatives-unranked-forkable

   Six nodes holding his own founding vision were unreachable from his own description of it, because BM25 is lexical and "go back to the decision point" shares no token with "fork". This is point 4's convergence clause, failing on a single-author graph rather than a forty-author corpus — which is a stronger case than the one the node has been carrying.

9. **AND EDGES DO NOT HELP, MEASURED THE SAME DAY.** `search_design` does not traverse. Two nodes linked ANTICIPATES an hour earlier: searching text unique to one returned it at 32.9 and the other did not appear in the top eight. So reflow2 holds a graph and a text index and composes them almost nowhere — `topic_report` reads each hit's connections, and that is the whole of it.

10. ⭐ **A THIRD OPTION, AND THE NODE HAS BEEN FRAMED AS A BINARY.** Every update above asks embeddings-plus-HNSW OR lexical. A survey of GraphRAG architectures (Towards Data Science, read 2026-09-22) names a shape neither branch covers: **GRAPH-FIRST retrieval** — traverse the graph to the region that satisfies the relational question, THEN restrict the text search to that neighbourhood, so lexical matching only has to work inside a set the graph already narrowed.
    · It needs **no model, no sidecar, no ONNX runtime** — so `req:thin-install` is untouched.
    · Graph traversal is **deterministic**, so the objection in point 5 that is strong for gates does not apply.
    · It costs **nothing in the export**, where point 2's sizing put full-precision vectors at more than double.
    · Every input exists today: the edges, the text index, and `topic_report` already does a one-hop version of it.

    🛑 **AND THE HONEST LIMIT, WHICH IS WHY THIS DOES NOT REPLACE EMBEDDINGS.** Graph-first needs a SEED. It makes one lucky lexical hit expand into a neighbourhood; it cannot start when no hit is lucky. On 2026-09-22 the lifecycle cluster WAS retrievable from Anthony's wording, so a graph expansion from those hits might have reached the fork cluster through shared neighbours — but that is a hypothesis, and it is cheap to test against the existing graph rather than argue. **Embeddings fix the FIRST hop; graph-first reduces how often the first hop has to be lucky.** They are complementary, and the cheaper one has never been tried.

11. **WHAT THE SURVEY ADDS TO POINT 6, AND WHAT IT TAKES AWAY.** Point 6 established that every comparable system is hybrid. The survey sharpens it: "hybrid" is not one decision but at least four distinct compositions — parallel dual retrieval, graph-first, vector-first, and a router that picks per query — with materially different costs. Parallel is explicitly called "token heavy… injecting redundant context"; the sequential shapes use one mode's output to narrow the other. So point 6's unanimity argues for COMPOSING the two halves, and says nothing about which composition.

12. ⚠️ **AND IT NAMES `relation_candidates`' MEASURED FAILURE MODE, WORD FOR WORD.** The vector-first pattern's stated trade-off is "Context Bloat — graph expansion from multiple seeds produces potentially thousands of irrelevant edges requiring careful scope limiting." Measured here 2026-09-22: four of five candidates offered for one node were justified by "both relate to `who:claude-code`" — an authorship hub nearly every recent node carries. The tool rarity-weights its TERMS and not its NEIGHBOURS. So scope limiting is not a detail of any graph-first or vector-first design here; it is the hard part, and this project already has a measured instance of getting it wrong.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 adopt embeddings and the HNSW index, or stay on lexical search?
properties.rationale: Captured because the review found the HNSW index entirely unused and the question live only in prose. The honest status is "already parked, now visible" rather than "newly proposed". Updated 2026-08-04 after BL-186 forced the question in practice: the findings above are measured against the local checkouts of embeddings-rs and dynograph-foundation rather than recalled, and the per-path determinism distinction is new. Anthony's scoping call — BL-186 ships lexical — is recorded here so the decision to defer is visible on the node itself rather than only in the increment that deferred it. Updated 2026-08-06 with the first EXTERNAL datum: the whole comparable field is hybrid graph-plus-vector, which removes one leg of the case-against without touching the determinism or thin-install legs.
